method: Independent current-source review of all 198 exact assigned files, including every gateway/core implementation and assigned test, every Web component/hook/library, all Web tests, all styles, HTML entry, TypeScript/Vite configuration and assigned verification documentation. Files were read in full with line numbers; long or truncated output was reread in bounded chunks. Reviewed authentication, exact Host/Origin and CSRF checks, session expiry and WebSocket ownership, channel registration and disconnect fencing, durable receipt transitions and recovery, scope/epoch ownership, resource limits, scheduler and worktree proof validation. Traced frontend mutation preflight, local storage/draft retention, asynchronous response ownership, subscription and terminal recovery, destructive-action confirmation, accessible labels, mobile layouts and discoverability across the complete current UI. Compared implementation invariants with every assigned test rather than inferring cleanliness from passing tests. Read the root instructions and the current test runner, selector, snapshot and release-audit implementation before the bounded validations. Reproductions transpile the unchanged current TS/TSX component dependency graph with the installed Vite transformer into .work and render those components in JSDOM with local simulated API/file responses. They do not duplicate component logic, invoke real shell commands, modify actual worktrees, contact MCP services or use personal configuration. Targeted tests were run only through the required runner; one failing file alone was rerun to investigate its failure. All source/test/documentation/feature-evidence files remained frozen; only .work diagnostics and this new audit artifact were written.
inspectionTopics: Gateway login, cookie/session/CSRF and Host/Origin validation; WebSocket session/lease ownership; private identifiers and disconnect cleanup.
Gateway-manager-worker RPC boundaries, request budgets, timeouts, durable pending/dispatching/unknown receipts and no automatic replay.
Automation schedule/timezone/concurrency behavior; worktree identity and positive completion proof; method and project/thread validation.
Web app navigation, active resource ownership, epoch/lease invalidation, late asynchronous reads, input drafts and accepted-operation reconciliation.
Approvals and input forms, MCP configuration/tools/resources/streams, skill import and discovery, process/terminal/realtime panels and lifecycle.
Workspace editor/conflicts/backups/index/commits/worktrees/download/search, history/fork/review/queue/agents, organization and sharing workflows.
All assigned tests, styles, responsive behavior, labels/templates, bounded displayed state and resource recovery; tests examined for missing temporal and consent-scope cases.

findings.title: Late skill import overwrites text entered while the file is loading
findings.trigger: Start importing a local SKILL.md, then edit the enabled skill-description textarea before file.arrayBuffer() resolves in the same project and epoch.
findings.impact: The import completion unconditionally replaces the newer manually entered description. The preparation step has not persisted a file draft yet, so this overwrites unsaved user work without a recovery draft. Track the draft revision when import starts, or explicitly prevent/resolve edits during the pending import.
findings.evidence: Current source checks only owner.current === key before setText(body); textarea onChange remains enabled and does not change that owner token. .work/round8/interface-repro.mjs case skill-import-overwrites-new-edit records beforeCompletion="new manually typed draft", afterCompletion="imported old text", recoveryDraftCount=0. The existing skill-library file passed all 9 tests but does not cover same-owner edits during a file read.

findings.title: Worktree creation consent also authorizes the open archive form
findings.trigger: Select an active managed worktree, expand the create-worktree form, open the archive confirmation for the selected tree, and check only the create-from-Git-reference confirmation.
findings.impact: Both forms share the single confirmed state from line 11. Checking the creation checkbox also checks the archive checkbox and enables archive; clicking its action sends workspace/worktree/archive with confirm:true even though the user never affirmed that separate archive intent. Keep confirmation scoped to the active action or make the forms mutually exclusive.
findings.evidence: The archive/attach/restore buttons set intent but do not close creating. Both confirmation inputs bind to confirmed. .work/round8/interface-repro.mjs case worktree-create-consent-enables-archive captured archiveConsentClicked=false, archiveConsentAfterCreateChecked=true and a simulated workspace/worktree/archive request with expectedRevision and confirm:true. The existing workspace-management file passed all 10 tests and lacks simultaneous-form coverage.

findings.title: An earlier shell acknowledgement clears a newer draft with equal text
findings.trigger: Submit shell command A, edit the still-enabled textarea to B and then back to A while the first request is awaiting acknowledgement, preparing another invocation.
findings.impact: The old acknowledgement clears the new draft because it compares only current text with submitted text. It does not establish that the draft has not been edited since submission. Preserve draft revision identity, as text equality alone cannot distinguish the later input generation.
findings.evidence: .work/round8/interface-repro.mjs case shell-ack-clears-new-aba-draft captured beforeAcknowledgement="echo repeat", afterAcknowledgement="", dispatchedCommands=1. Source line 40 uses setCommand(current => current === submitted ? "" : current). The existing newer-edit test only changes the value to a different string and therefore misses the A-to-B-to-A case.

findings.title: Changing MCP server retains consent for the previous event subscription
findings.trigger: Select MCP service A, enter a service-specific stream name and arguments, confirm starting that subscription, then select connected service B before submitting.
findings.impact: The select handler resets tool/resource state but leaves streamName, streamArguments and streamConsent intact. The start button remains enabled and submits the old service-specific parameters to B, although the checkbox consent was given for A. Reset or bind subscription consent to server/thread/lease and the exact submitted parameters.
findings.evidence: .work/round8/interface-followup-repro.mjs case mcp-stream-consent-survives-server-change records confirmedServer="first", submittedServer="second", consentStillChecked=true and an actual component beginMutation("mcp/stream/start") call to second with {scope:"first-only"}. The lease/thread reset effect on line 37 also omits this consent. Existing mcp-ui tests all 12 passed but do not exercise this stream selection transition.

validations.setupCorrection: Initial execution failed because the local MCP fixture omitted the mcp/config/read catalog shape. The fixture alone was corrected; the successful execution used current unchanged source.

limitations: Full-suite execution is prohibited before the audit gate and was not started. No full-suite pass is claimed.

No SSH, browser automation, deployed/native live integration, model inference, external MCP service or personal configuration was used. JSDOM fixtures establish the reported component state transitions, not deployment or visual-browser completeness.

The existing whole-thread cleanup test in web/tests/thread-terminals.test.tsx failed both the initial selected run and the isolated rerun, while its five sibling tests passed. It timed out looking for the accepted-cleanup notice. A separate local component trace reached one cleanup mutation; the discrepancy was not diagnosed to a confirmed product root cause. Both failed runs remain explicitly recorded and this audit does not claim all selected tests passed.

Inspection of installed dependency API shape was limited to Vite export introspection and the transformWithOxc declaration at node_modules/vite/dist/node/index.d.ts:3277, plus a TypeScript transpileModule availability probe. Third-party package implementation was not audited.

Reading assigned web/VERIFICATION.md necessarily exposed its historical implementation and prior-round summaries. No linked previous report/evidence was opened, no audits.json was read, and those summaries were not used as a finding guide. No old/sibling repository or Git history was consulted.
